LIERARY
Mobility Studies
Lincoln Highway Improvement
Cicero Avenue to Chicago Road
Cook County
July 8, 1971
Mr. George R. Bonick, Mayor City of Chicago Heights 1430 Chicago Road Chicago Heights, Illinois 60411
Dear Mr. Fonick:
On June 30, 1971, we sent to your office a strip map which represents our current thinking for the improvement of Lincoln Highway between Cicero Avenue and Chicago Road. As you may have noticed from these plans, we are proposing to acquire from the Roosevelt School a strip of land a portion of which is used for macreational purposes (see attachment). The Division's policy requires that in such takings we examine the possibility and practicality of replacing these recreational lands takings.
To this end we are submitting for your City's review four schemes all of which require the use of a portion of Sunnyside Avenue for this recreational land replacement, however, the one question that is primary in our mind is whether or not the closure of Sunnyside Avenue at Lincoln Highway is acceptable to the City of Chicago Heights. If it is not, then we feel that there are not any feasible solutions to this replacement problem. If it is, then we are requesting that you review those four schemes and comment on the desirability and acceptability of each.
The four schemes can be described as follows:
Scheme A shows the provision of a large cul-de-sac on Sunmyside Street north of the school building. The taking from the area north of the building is 3,695 square feet and the taking from the playground area west of the school is 3,530 square feet. By closing a portion of Sunmyside Street, 8,100 square feet are added to the playground area. This yields a gain of 275 square feet for playground space and a net loss of 4,385 square feet of school property. The large cul-de-sac would enable Sunmyside Street to be used as a secondary point of access to the school.
